title: EPC-W5-GR Architecture Review Go/No-Go

confirmedFindings: Master Catalog is the canonical backend owner.
Compatibility and fallback paths still exist in the frontend and simulation surfaces.
The absence of the enterprise-context SSOT remains a governance gap.
The dependency graph correctly separates canonical-core, shadow-read, compatibility, and legacy edges.
Commercial Coverage still depends on a shadow comparison against creditPfCatalog.
loan-with-collateral still carries aliases and fallback behavior.
Oportunidades remains the first candidate, but deferred pending gates.
The cut plan is staged and rollback-aware.
The retirement posture still requires parity proof and release gates.

candidateReview.reason: It is still the best first candidate, but it cannot be authorized until the observability and parity gates exist.

rollbackPaths: restore shadow read for Commercial Coverage
restore compatibility alias resolution for loan-with-collateral
keep empty-tree error fallback for Oportunidades during controlled rollout

readinessDecisions.reason: The canonical core is ready, but the wave still requires controlled execution and no blanket retirement.
Observability prerequisites are the next authorized step and must precede any functional cut.
Oportunidades remains the first candidate, but it cannot be promoted until the gates and telemetry are in place.
The first functional cut is blocked until measurable observability and formal parity gates exist.
Legacy removal cannot proceed while compatibility paths and retirement proof are still required.
Fallback removal remains unsafe until alias-hit and lookup-miss evidence is zeroed out.
creditPfCatalog retirement is blocked until parity proof and a retirement gate are in place.

goNoGoMatrix.reason: Wave-level execution is allowed, but only with controlled rollout and no blanket retirement.
This is the next authorized step.
Still the best first candidate, but the gates are not ready.
No functional cut before measurable observability and parity gates exist.
Legacy removal is not authorized while compatibility paths remain live.
Fallback removal is not authorized while alias and fallback evidence remains active.
Retirement is not authorized without parity proof and a formal retirement gate.

blockers.impact: Governance closure is incomplete, but catalog execution is not automatically blocked.
Commercial Coverage, loan-with-collateral fallback removal, creditPfCatalog retirement, and legacy removal remain NO_GO.
No first functional cut may be authorized before observability and measurable gates exist.

findings.finding: The enterprise-context SSOT file is missing.
There is no formal measurable parity, shadow, and fallback gate for the first functional cut.
Commercial Coverage still depends on a shadow read against creditPfCatalog.
loan-with-collateral still uses aliases and fallback resolution.
Oportunidades remains the first candidate but must stay deferred pending gates.
Legacy removal is not ready because compatibility and retirement proof are still required.
creditPfCatalog retirement is not ready because parity proof and a formal retirement gate do not exist yet.

risks.name: Shadow comparison can mask permanent dependency on creditPfCatalog
Compatibility fallback can keep obsolete aliases alive longer than intended
Empty-tree fallback can hide availability issues if telemetry is weak
First functional cut without measurable gates would create an under-evidenced release

gaps.name: No formal measured parity baseline for shadow retirement
No retirement gate that binds observability to cutover

recommendations: Keep the canonical backend as the owner of truth.
Keep Commercial Coverage on shadow until parity is measured.
Delay retirement of compatibility fallbacks until the evidence is explicit.
